description: Take a real picture of the page under test, or of ONE element, and hand it back as an image you can look at — not as measurements. Use it for the questions geometry cannot answer: does this look right, is the shadow there, is the text legible on that background, what does the tester actually see. Pass `ref` or `selector` to crop to one element (with a little padding); omit both for the visible page. Pass `full: true` for THE WHOLE PAGE top to bottom, however long it is — the page is scrolled, photographed a screenful at a time and stitched into one picture, with a sticky header kept once rather than printed down the side. That is usually what a human means by "show me the page", and the visible-area shot answers a different question. It takes a second or so per screenful and cannot be combined with `ref`/`selector`. The Qiksy panel is hidden and password and card fields are covered BEFORE the frame is taken, so a screenshot pasted into a ticket carries no secret. THE TAB MUST BE IN FRONT: the browser photographs the window's active tab, and Qiksy refuses to photograph a different one rather than hand you a page you did not ask about — call qa_focus_tab first if you have been driving a background tab. A PICTURE OF THE PAGE IS NOT A PICTURE OF THE PERSON'S SCREEN: when Chrome is not the application in front, the reply carries `seenByHuman: false` and `screen`, and then the person is looking at something else. Say so; do not present the picture as what they see. EVERY SHOT CARRIES TWO THINGS A PICTURE CANNOT SAY ABOUT ITSELF: `build` — which build was actually running (the script files the page fetched, whatever version it declares, viewport, DPR, colour scheme, language), so nobody has to ask «which build was this»; and `receipt` — what was covered before the frame and what was never collected at all, which is what makes a picture of somebody else's application sendable. Downscaled to `maxWidth` (default 1200) because a retina frame is megabytes of context for pixels nobody needed. PASS `path` FOR A LONG PAGE: the file is written at FULL resolution — the downscale exists to protect this conversation, and a file is not this conversation. An inline thirty-screen shot is unreadable by arithmetic, not by accident. Read-only: it changes nothing on the page.

full.description: Photograph the WHOLE page, not just the visible part — scrolled and stitched. Ignored when ref/selector is given.

map.description: Return the element map with the picture: every visible control with its accessible name, role, CSS selector and box IN IMAGE PIXELS. This is what makes a screenshot something you can point INTO — anchor an annotation to a control, or draw a finding onto the shot without aiming. Written automatically beside the file when `path` is given.

maxWidth.description: Downscale to at most this wide (default 1200, max 2000)

path.description: Write the PNG here instead of returning it inline — an absolute path, or one relative to where the bridge runs. You get back the path and the size, at FULL resolution, plus a `<name>.map.json` beside it.

ref.description: Crop to this element (a ref from qa_snapshot)

searchable.description: Also write a searchable SVG beside the PNG: the same picture with every string the page was showing written invisibly over its own pixels, so Ctrl+F works INSIDE the screenshot and the text can be selected and copied. Not OCR — the strings were read from the live document, so there is no recognition to be wrong about. Text inside <canvas> or a frame cannot be included, and the file says so.

selector.description: Crop to the first element matching this CSS selector

tabId.description: Target tab (from qa_tabs); omit for the active tab

name: qa_screenshot
title: Screenshot the page or one element
